name: MEXICO

flag.title: Flag of México
flag.note: Green, white & red with eagle emblem

lead: Mexico sits at the bottom of North America. Snowy volcanoes tower over old pyramids. Jaguars hide in the jungle. Mexico gave the world chocolate, corn and colour television.
geo: Mexico has a spiny desert in the north. The Sierra Madre mountains run down its middle. Thick jungle grows in the south.
Mexico City sits 2,240 m above sea level. Visiting footballers struggle to breathe there. Mexico has 200 volcanoes. Of these, 48 are still active.
animals: A golden eagle sits on Mexico's flag. It can spot a rabbit two kilometres away. Whale sharks swim in the reefs off Yucatán.
The axolotl is a smiling water lizard with feathery gills. It never fully grows up and can regrow lost limbs. It lives only in the canals of Xochimilco, in Mexico City.
culture: Every November, families build flower altars for Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead). They visit candlelit graves to welcome their ancestors' spirits. It is joyful, with marigolds, music and favourite foods.
Mariachi bands in silver-studded suits play trumpets and violins. Street stalls sell tacos, tamales and buttered corn.
history: The Aztecs ruled from Tenochtitlan, an island city where Mexico City stands now. At its peak around 300,000 people lived there, trading gold and chocolate beans.
Spanish conqueror Hernán Cortés toppled the Aztecs in 1521. In 1810 priest Miguel Hidalgo rang his church bell to spark revolt. Mexico won independence in 1821.
wows: Cholula's pyramid is the world's biggest by size, with a church on top.
A colour-TV system invented in Mexico in 1940 later helped NASA get colour pictures of Jupiter.
Mexico City is sinking, with some spots down over 12 m in a century.
The Chihuahua, the world's tiniest dog, is named for a Mexican state bigger than the UK.
Hundreds of millions of monarch butterflies fly 4,500 km from Canada to Mexico each winter.
The Americas' first printing press arrived in Mexico City in 1539, centuries before most neighbours.
The Maya and Aztecs drank chocolate as a bitter spiced drink, with no sugar.

myths.myth: Cinco de Mayo is Mexico's Independence Day
myths.fact: No. Cinco de Mayo marks the 1862 win over France at Puebla. Independence Day is on 16 September.

myths.myth: All Mexican food is very spicy
myths.fact: Many dishes are mild. People add chilli sauce at the table if they like it hot.
